summary: The claim and proof are correct. The full-row counting identity gives exact conservation of the integer class excesses. Negative-excess classes have a uniform positive energy gap, while zero-excess classes admit the stated quadratic score estimate, with compactness used only away from their explicitly characterized zeros. These facts control all pair scores without a midpoint multiplicity bound, and the entire-center estimates yield the claimed logarithmic price. The full-row and original-probability normalizations agree with the supplied predecessor facts, and all reused identities are also established directly under the present hypotheses. The halfspace argument, auxiliary-center factorization, and product optimization prove the stated moment bounds with the coefficient paid once. Singleton supports, absent pairs, balanced-interval endpoints, vanishing scores, and lower-dimensional supports are covered without gaps.
